anchor_definition: The anchor is the slide-captcha success callback for password login (an anonymous function in loginbypassword20231031.js, reached via initSlideMathCode): it validates the username/password, then assembles jQuery.ajax({ url:'/loginwithpwdStrong.api', data:{ uid, pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, password), ... } }) and POSTs it. It is the complete function in which the captured 1.json code (loginbypassword20231031.js:369) appears. encryptedString is the generic RSA primitive it calls directly (Core utility 0.5) — there is no dedicated app-level password encryptor, so no 0.7 helper exists.

anchor.why: The slide-captcha success callback (password login): validates username/password, then assembles jQuery.ajax({url:'/loginwithpwdStrong.api', data:{uid, pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, that.password.val()), ...}}) and POSTs it. The complete (anonymous) function containing the captured 1.json code where the pwd field is written. Reached via initSlideMathCode, which sets up the captcha and contains this callback (so initSlideMathCode also scores 1.0 by containment).

roles.why: The generic RSA string-encryption primitive (RSA.min.js): block-splits the input and exponentiates with the given RSAKeyPair. Called directly by the anchor as encryptedString(key_to_encode, password) to produce the pwd token; reusable library routine, not bound to this login.
Generic RSA key-pair constructor (RSA.min.js): builds the RSAKeyPair (exponent/modulus BigInts, chunk sizing) consumed by encryptedString. Reusable crypto primitive on the construction path.
Generic BigInt multiplication used inside RSA modular exponentiation; a low-level math helper deep on the construction path, not the token constructor.
The inverse RSA decryption routine; never on the password-encryption path. A pure decoy.

empty_roles.reason: There is no dedicated app-level password encryptor: the anchor calls the generic RSA primitive directly as encryptedString(key_to_encode, password), so no target-specific helper sits between the anchor and the library primitive to award 0.7.

The captcha-verified login is reached indirectly: a first /loginwithpwdStrong.api attempt's success handler, on high error count, calls initSlideMathCode, whose slide-captcha success callback is the anchor. initSlideMathCode contains the anchor (so it scores 1.0 by containment, not 0.2), and there is no separate single app-level function that directly calls the anchor to award 0.2.
